Team — summary from customer: intermittent token stalls ~4–8s starting ~09:05 UTC in us-west-2; session id 9f3b attached. Priority: high (live UX impact, business conversions).

Immediate triage steps (please action in parallel):
1) Karthik: run a 30-min tail-latency sweep for streaming endpoints in us-west-2 across GPU pool fleet (seqlen distribution, kernel selection shifts, and recent quantization flags). Collect top 50 request_ids by latency and share S3 link.

Suggested immediate mitigations to propose to customer (we can tailor after Karthik’s traces):

Subject: Update & temporary playbook — QuickServe streaming latency incident

Theo / Sabrina — final update from our investigation and suggested customer actions. Thanks again for the trace sample; that made root-cause correlation much faster.

What we found (summary):
- Root cause: transient kernel-selection oscillation on a subset of us-west-2 inference nodes after a background kernel probe at ~09:03 UTC. The probe caused per-request scheduling jitter for requests crossing a quantized KV-cache boundary; manifests as token-delivery stalls of several seconds.
- Impact window: ~09:03–10:40 UTC; >95% of requests unaffected but a small percentage (0.8% of streaming sessions) experienced visible stutter.
- Remediation performed: we rolled back the kernel probe roll and applied a conservative kernel-cache affinity patch; autoscaler did not contribute.

Customer-facing mitigation checklist (short-term):
1) Client fallbacks (recommended now):
   - Enable a 200–500ms client buffer for streaming frames (smooths UX for micro-stalls).
   - Add exponential-backoff retry for frame timeouts >6s with jitter (max 3 retries).
   - If uninterrupted streaming is critical, temporarily switch to the non-streaming /generate endpoint for high-concurrency flows (we see slightly higher end-to-end latency but no token-level stutter).
2) Server config suggestions (we can make these on your behalf):
   - Route high-sensitivity sessions to the low-latency model variant (model-lowlat-v2) for the next 48 hours.
   - If you use pinned model versions, we can provision a small dedicated pool for your critical traffic to isolate kernel selection variability.
3) Operational goodies we’ll provide:
   - We’ve attached a short runbook and a CSV timeline of the event.
   - We’ll share detailed traces for the affected request_ids (traces_9f3b.zip) and a short postmortem within 72 hours.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Karthik and our infra team will produce a short technical postmortem (kernel probe parameters and patch) and a permanent fix schedule within 72 hours.
- Monica will follow up on credits/contract remediation if you’d like; she’ll propose an amount based on impacted sessions.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute sync with our SRE + your platform team this afternoon to walk the traces and runbook. Would 16:00 UTC work?

Thanks for your patience — we know live chat quality is business-critical.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
